result.summary: This residential intersection lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control devices. While sidewalks are present on both sides of the street, the wide, unmarked roadway and presence of parked cars near the corners create significant exposure and visibility challenges for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to designate a safe crossing area for pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled intersection
hazards.description: No stop signs or traffic signals are visible to regulate vehicle right-of-way at the crossing point.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile warning strips and sloped ramps at all intersection corners for accessibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked roadway that lacks designated crossing points and traffic calming measures. While a sidewalk is present on the right side, the left side lacks a paved walkway, and the overall design prioritizes vehicular movement over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross this wide roadway, increasing exposure risk.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide road can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.

hazards.name: Incomplete sidewalk network
hazards.description: The sidewalk is only present on the right side, forcing pedestrians on the left to walk in the grass or the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Road Diet
interventions.description: Add lane markings to narrow travel lanes and slow traffic speeds through visual cues.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, separated walking path.

result.summary: The image depicts an industrial or commercial environment with a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass verge. A large semi-truck is positioned in the foreground, creating a significant visual obstruction for pedestrians and drivers alike.
